def strip_stop_strings(texts: list[str], stop_strings: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Truncate each text at the first occurrence of any stop string.

    Args:
        texts: The list of generated texts to clean.
        stop_strings: Stop strings that mark the end of useful content.

    Returns:

    if not texts:

    result: list[str] = []
    for text in texts:

        for stop in stop_strings:

## Summary

Implemented four functions across three new source files (no `tests/` files touched):

**`docling/utils/chandra_utils.py`** — `parse_chandra_html(content, original_page_size, page_no, filename)`
- Selects top-level `<div>` blocks with `data-bbox`+`data-label` (excludes divs nested inside another labeled block, so List-Group items aren't double-counted).
- Maps labels to `DocItemLabel` via a case-insensitive map, defaulting unknown labels to `TEXT`.
- Normalizes bboxes from 0–1000 space to page coords, clamping to non-negative values; every text item gets a provenance entry.
- Parses inner HTML for `Table` divs, expands `List-Group` divs into individual list items (using per-item bboxes when present), routes `Title`/`Section-Header`/`Code`/`Picture` to the right add methods.
- Skips divs with missing/invalid attributes or non-numeric bboxes; returns an empty doc for empty/whitespace content.

**`docling/utils/dots_utils.py`** — `parse_dots_json(...)` and `_clean_json(...)`
- Runs content through `_clean_json`, parses the JSON array, maps the 11 dots.ocr categories to labels (unknown → `TEXT`).
- Rescales bboxes from `model_image_size` to the page when provided; parses HTML for `Table` items; adds pictures/titles/headings/list-items appropriately.
- Skips non-dict elements and invalid bboxes; returns an empty doc for empty/whitespace/invalid JSON.
- `_clean_json`: returns input unchanged if already valid, `'[]'` if no `[`, otherwise strips leading text before the first `[`, drops the incomplete trailing element, and closes the array.

**`docling/utils/vlm_utils.py`** — `strip_stop_strings(...)` and `compute_qwen2vl_image_size(...)`
- `strip_stop_strings`: truncates each text at the earliest stop-string match; leaves text unchanged when none matches; `[]` for empty input.
- `compute_qwen2vl_image_size`: applies `scale`, clamps to `max_size`, rounds dimensions to multiples of `factor`, then floors/ceils to keep total area within `[min_pixels, max_pixels]` (Qwen2-VL-style defaults). Returns a `Size`.

One judgment call worth flagging: the exact default numeric values for `compute_qwen2vl_image_size` (`max_size`, `max_pixels`, `min_pixels`, `factor`) aren't specified in the task, so I used standard Qwen2-VL conventions (`factor=28`, `min_pixels=4·28²`, `max_pixels=1280·28²`, `max_size=3584`).
